  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

21118	def check_hpap(
21119	    proof: HPAP,
21120	    signature: AggregateSignature,
21121	    key: SigningDKGResult,
21122	) -> bool:
21123	    """Rebuild a proof's Merkle root and verify its bundles and root signature.
21124

21126	    Each disclosed bundle's leaf digest is then recomputed from its
21127	    position and the bundle exactly as in :func:`make_hpap`, and the
21128	    root is rebuilt level by level while consuming ``proof.siblings`` in
21129	    ascending level order and left to right within a level: the current
21130	    level holds the digests of the proven nodes at their current
21131	    positions, paired left to right; when a companion is itself a
21132	    current-level node its digest is used directly, when the node is the
21133	    last member of an odd-width level it is paired with itself, and
21134	    otherwise the next 32-byte entry of ``siblings`` is consumed. The
21135	    current width contracts as ``(width + 1) // 2`` and the rebuild must
21136	    consume every sibling exactly. Every disclosed bundle is then
21137	    re-checked with :func:`verify_hpb` against ``key`` in index order,
21138	    so each bundle's nested HP proof and every archive proof bundle it
21139	    in turn discloses must verify, and the statement
21140	    ``b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root`` is finally checked as
21141	    ``signature``'s threshold Schnorr message via
21142	    :func:`verify_signature` with the key's group parameters. Returns
21143	    ``True`` only when the rebuild consumes every sibling exactly and
21144	    reaches the single signed root, every bundle verifies against the
21145	    key and the signature verifies; a well-formed proof whose bundles,
21146	    indices, siblings, root or signature was tampered with — bundles
21147	    swapped or altered, a bundle, index or sibling missing or extra, a
21148	    misplaced sibling — or which is presented under another key, returns
21149	    ``False`` rather than raising.
21150	
21151	    A non-:class:`HPAP` or non-:class:`AggregateSignature` argument or
21152	    any wrong field type (non-tuple indices/bundles/siblings, a
21153	    non-integer ``total`` or index including booleans, a non-:class:`HPB`
21154	    bundle or non-bytes sibling) raises TypeError; a non-positive or
21155	    over-64-bit ``total``, empty indices, an index out of range or not
21156	    strictly increasing, a sibling entry that is not exactly 32 bytes, or
21157	    a structurally illegal bundle, signature or ``key`` raises ValueError,
21158	    exactly as :func:`verify_hpb` and :func:`verify_signature` would.
21159	    """

21161	    if not isinstance(signature, AggregateSignature):
21162	        raise TypeError("signature must be an AggregateSignature instance")

21176	        for index, bundle in zip(indices, bundles)

21180	    while width > 1:

21182	        for position in sorted(nodes):

21185	                continue

21189	                    nodes[position], nodes[position]

21204	                    )

21239	# with the aggregate threshold-Schnorr signature over its root statement

21243	# bundle or signature is checked and no state is kept, so check_hpap
21244	# through verify_hpapb remains the sole verifier afterwards.

21247	HPAP_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpap/v1"
21248	HPAPB_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpapb/v1"

21251	def encode_hpap(proof: HPAP) -> bytes:
21252	    """Canonically encode an HPAP membership proof for transport or persistence.
21253	
21254	    The encoding is the direct concatenation, in order, of the tag
21255	    ``b"ts/hpap/v1"``, ``VARINT(total)``, the index count as a 4-byte
21256	    unsigned big-endian integer, one ``VARINT(index)`` per proven leaf in
21257	    the proof's strictly increasing order, the bundle count as a 4-byte
21258	    unsigned big-endian integer, one frame per bundle — the 4-byte
21259	    unsigned big-endian length ``len(E)`` followed by the raw bytes
21260	    ``E = encode_hpb(bundle_value)`` (never empty) — and a 4-byte unsigned
21261	    big-endian sibling item count followed by the raw 32-byte sibling
21262	    digests concatenated directly in their original leaf-to-root,
21263	    left-to-right order. A ``VARINT`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian body
21264	    length followed by the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the
21265	    single byte ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero). The
21266	    integer and frame conventions are exactly those of :func:`encode_hp`.
21267	    The indices must be non-empty, strictly increasing, unique and within
21268	    ``0 <= i < total``, the bundle count must equal the index count, and
21269	    the sibling count must be the unique one derived from ``total`` and
21270	    the indices by the compact multi-proof walk.
21271	
21272	    Only a structurally legal :class:`HPAP` is accepted — a non-:class:`HPAP`
21273	    argument or wrong field types raise TypeError and illegal bounds, an
21274	    empty index tuple, a bundle tuple that does not pair one-to-one with
21275	    the indices, a sibling that is not exactly 32 bytes, a sibling count
21276	    other than the one ``total`` and the indices determine, a
21277	    structurally illegal nested bundle or an over-long frame raises
21278	    ValueError — but the bundles are not verified and no signature is
21279	    involved: :func:`check_hpap` stays the way to verify a proof
21280	    afterwards. The output for a given proof is unique and the encoding
21281	    carries no network, storage or hidden state.
21282	    """
21283	    indices, total, bundles, siblings = _validate_hpap_structure(proof)
21284	    try:
21285	        if len(bundles) != len(indices):
21286	            raise ValueError(
21287	                "proof.bundles must pair one-to-one with proof.indices"
21288	            )
21289	    except OverflowError:
21290	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive proof bundles") from None
21291	    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
21292	        total, indices
21293	    )
21294	    if len(siblings) != required_siblings:
21295	        raise ValueError(
21296	            "proof.siblings count is not the one determined by total "
21297	            "and indices"
21298	        )
21299	    if len(indices) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
21300	        raise ValueError("too many indices")
21301	    if len(siblings) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
21302	        raise ValueError("too many siblings")
21303	
21304	    encoded_bundles = []
21305	    for position, bundle_value in enumerate(bundles):
21306	        encoded_bundle = encode_hpb(bundle_value)
21307	        if len(encoded_bundle) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
21308	            raise ValueError(
21309	                f"hpap bundle {position + 1} encoding too long"
21310	            )
21311	        encoded_bundles.append(encoded_bundle)
21312	
21313	    buffer = bytearray(HPAP_WIRE_TAG)
21314	    buffer += _encode_varint(total)
21315	    buffer += len(indices).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
21316	    for index in indices:
21317	        buffer += _encode_varint(index)
21318	    buffer += len(encoded_bundles).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
21319	    for encoded_bundle in encoded_bundles:
21320	        buffer += len(encoded_bundle).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
21321	        buffer += encoded_bundle
21322	    buffer += len(siblings).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
21323	    for sibling in siblings:
21324	        buffer += sibling
21325	    return bytes(buffer)

21328	def decode_hpap(blob: bytes) -> HPAP:
21329	    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpap`.
21330	
21331	    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag ``b"ts/hpap/v1"``, the
21332	    length-prefixed integer ``total`` (a 4-byte unsigned big-endian
21333	    length followed by its shortest unsigned big-endian value, zero
21334	    encoded as the single byte ``00``), the 4-byte non-zero index count
21335	    followed by one canonical ``VARINT`` per strictly increasing index,
21336	    the 4-byte bundle count (which must equal the index count) followed
21337	    by that many non-empty bundle frames (a 4-byte non-zero length
21338	    followed by bytes that :func:`decode_hpb` accepts), and the 4-byte
21339	    sibling item count followed by exactly that many raw 32-byte sibling
21340	    digests concatenated with no further framing, where the count must be
21341	    the unique one derived from ``total`` and the disclosed indices. A
21342	    non-bytes argument raises TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, an empty
21343	    index list, a non-positive or over-64-bit ``total``, an index outside
21344	    ``0 <= i < total``, indices that are not strictly increasing and
21345	    unique, a bundle count that does not match the index count, an empty,
21346	    truncated or non-canonical bundle frame, a missing or extra sibling
21347	    relative to the count ``total`` and the indices require, a sibling
21348	    section whose width is not exactly 32 bytes per item, a non-canonical
21349	    integer (leading zero or over-long length), truncation, or trailing
21350	    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded proof re-encodes to
21351	    exactly the input bytes.
21352	
21353	    Decoding only restores the structure: each nested bundle is decoded
21354	    with :func:`decode_hpb` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
21355	    signature). A structurally legal proof whose nested bundles do not
21356	    verify is returned normally, and :func:`check_hpap` reports it as
21357	    ``False``.
21358	    """
21359	    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
21360	        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
21361	    if not blob.startswith(HPAP_WIRE_TAG):
21362	        raise ValueError("bad HPAP proof tag")
21363	    offset = len(HPAP_WIRE_TAG)
21364	
21365	    total, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="hpap proof total")
21366	    if total <= 0:
21367	        raise ValueError("hpap proof total must be positive")
21368	    if total > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:
21369	        raise ValueError("hpap proof total too large")
21370	
21371	    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
21372	        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof index count")
21373	    index_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
21374	    offset += 4
21375	    if index_count == 0:
21376	        raise ValueError("hpap proof indices must be non-empty")
21377	    indices = []
21378	    for _ in range(index_count):
21379	        index, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="hpap proof index")
21380	        indices.append(index)
21381	
21382	    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
21383	        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof bundle count")
21384	    bundle_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
21385	    offset += 4
21386	    if bundle_count != index_count:
21387	        raise ValueError(
21388	            "hpap proof bundle count must match the index count"
21389	        )
21390	    bundles = []
21391	    for position in range(bundle_count):
21392	        encoded_bundle, offset = _read_archive_block(
21393	            blob,
21394	            offset,
21395	            what=f"hpap proof bundle {position + 1}",
21396	        )
21397	        bundles.append(decode_hpb(encoded_bundle))
21398	
21399	    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
21400	        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof sibling count")
21401	    sibling_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
21402	    offset += 4
21403	    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
21404	        total, tuple(indices)
21405	    )
21406	    if sibling_count != required_siblings:
21407	        raise ValueError(
21408	            "hpap proof sibling count is not the one determined by total "
21409	            "and indices"
21410	        )
21411	    siblings = []
21412	    for _ in range(sibling_count):
21413	        if offset + HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE > len(blob):
21414	            raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof sibling")
21415	        siblings.append(
21416	            bytes(blob[offset:offset + HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE])
21417	        )
21418	        offset += HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE
21419	
21420	    if offset != len(blob):
21421	        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPAP proof")
21422	
21423	    proof = HPAP(
21424	        indices=tuple(indices),
21425	        total=total,
21426	        bundles=tuple(bundles),
21427	        siblings=tuple(siblings),
21428	    )
21429	    _validate_hpap_structure(proof)
21430	    if encode_hpap(proof) != blob:
21431	        raise ValueError("non-canonical hpap proof encoding")
21432	    return proof

21453	def encode_hpapb(bundle: HPAPB) -> bytes:

21457	    ``b"ts/hpapb/v1"``, one 4-byte unsigned big-endian length frame whose
21458	    body is exactly ``encode_hpap(bundle.proof)`` (never empty), and then
21459	    the existing signature frame: ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compact multi-bundle membership proofs over an HPB archive: one threshold
# signature on the Merkle root statement authenticates any subset of the
# archive's HPB transport bundles at once. The tree is exactly isomorphic to
# the HP membership proof tree one level down — leaves bind each position to
# the bundle's existing canonical encode_hpb bytes, an odd tail pairs with
# itself, and positions and counts are 8-byte unsigned big-endian — only the
# domain tags and the nested bundle type change. The proof value is a frozen
# value and no state is kept: check_hpap remains the sole verifier. The
# canonical transport encoding (encode_hpap) and the proof-plus-root-
# signature bundle (HPAPB / encode_hpapb) follow one layer below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

HPAP_LEAF_TAG = b"hpap/l"
HPAP_NODE_TAG = b"hpap/n"
HPAP_ROOT_TAG = b"hpap/r"

HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE = 32  # SHA256 width; every tree node is this wide


def _hpap_leaf(index: int, bundle: HPB) -> bytes:
    """The index-bound leaf digest ``H(b"hpap/l" || U64(i) || H(encode_hpb(bundle)))``."""
    return hashlib.sha256(
        HPAP_LEAF_TAG
        + _hp_u64(index)
        + hashlib.sha256(encode_hpb(bundle)).digest()
    ).digest()


def _hpap_node(left: bytes, right: bytes) -> bytes:
    """The ordered internal digest ``H(b"hpap/n" || left || right)``."""
    return hashlib.sha256(HPAP_NODE_TAG + left + right).digest()


def _hpap_levels(
    bundles: tuple[HPB, ...],
) -> list[tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Build the leaf level and every internal level up to the single root.

    A level with an odd tail width is paired with its own last node
    duplicated, so every level above the leaves has an even width.
    """
    levels: list[tuple[bytes, ...]] = [
        tuple(
            _hpap_leaf(index, bundle)
            for index, bundle in enumerate(bundles)
        )
    ]
    current = levels[0]
    while len(current) > 1:
        if len(current) % 2 == 1:
            current = current + current[-1:]
        current = tuple(
            _hpap_node(current[index], current[index + 1])
            for index in range(0, len(current), 2)
        )
        levels.append(current)
    return levels


def _check_hpap_archive_items(
    items: object,
) -> tuple[HPB, ...]:
    """Type- and structure-check a non-empty ordered tuple of HPB bundles.

    Mirrors the container and per-item checks the archive codec applies
    to ``items``: a tuple of :class:`HPB` instances, non-empty, each
    structurally legal through its own canonical encoder. The archive's
    outer signature is deliberately outside the scope — the proof is
    built from the bundles alone. Nothing here verifies any signature.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
            raise TypeError(
                "each archive item must be an HPB instance"
            )
    try:
        count = len(items)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
    if count == 0:
        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
    # Encode every bundle first — each call raises TypeError/ValueError
    # for an illegal bundle exactly as the bundle codec does — so a
    # single illegal item aborts the whole proof.
    for item in items:
        encode_hpb(item)
    return items


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HPAP:
    """A compact Merkle membership proof for several bundles of an HPB archive.

    The fields, in order, are ``indices`` (the proven leaf positions as a
    non-empty tuple of strictly increasing, unique non-negative integers),
    ``total`` (the total, non-empty archive bundle count), ``bundles``
    (the proven :class:`HPB` values, one per entry of ``indices``, in
    the same order) and ``siblings`` (the 32-byte sibling digests consumed
    from the leaf level up to the root, in ascending level order and left
    to right within a level; the tuple is empty when no sibling digests
    are needed). At a level whose width is odd, the last node pairs with
    itself and no sibling is carried for it, and a companion that is
    itself a disclosed node is never carried either; the number and order
    of siblings are therefore fixed uniquely by ``total`` and ``indices``.
    The dataclass is frozen, positionally constructible and compared by
    value, and carries no network, storage or hidden state. Field types
    and bounds are not checked at construction time — :func:`check_hpap`
    is the way to test a proof afterwards.
    """

    indices: tuple[int, ...]
    total: int
    bundles: tuple[HPB, ...]
    siblings: tuple[bytes, ...]


def make_hpap(
    archive: HPBArchive, indices: tuple[int, ...]
) -> tuple[bytes, HPAP]:
    """Build the root statement and a compact multi-bundle membership proof.

    ``archive`` must be an :class:`HPBArchive` whose items are a
    non-empty tuple of structurally legal :class:`HPB` values exactly
    as :func:`encode_hpb` requires, and ``indices`` a non-empty tuple
    of leaf positions to prove. Only the archive's structure and its
    bundles are consulted: the archive's own outer signature is never
    examined and no state is kept. The tree is built in archive order
    with SHA256, exactly isomorphic to the HP membership proof tree:
    leaves are ``H(b"hpap/l" || U64(i) || H(encode_hpb(bundle)))`` and
    internal nodes ``H(b"hpap/n" || left || right)``; a level with an
    odd tail width duplicates its last node for pairing, and positions
    and counts are encoded as 8-byte unsigned big-endian integers.
    Returns ``(message, proof)`` where ``message`` is
    ``b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root`` (the 8-byte unsigned big-endian
    bundle count followed by the 32-byte root) — the bytes to be
    threshold-signed through the caller's two-round signing flow — and
    ``proof`` is the :class:`HPAP` whose ``bundles`` take the archive
    items at ``indices`` in archive order, one to one. Its ``siblings``
    are collected level by level, in ascending level order (leaves
    upward) and left to right within a level, one entry per needed
    companion: when the companion position is itself a proven node
    carried in the proof, or the node is the last member of an odd-width
    level (paired with itself), no sibling is appended; otherwise the
    companion digest is. Proven nodes from lower levels feed the level
    above exactly as in the tree, so no digest is sent twice. One
    threshold signature over the statement covers every index subset of
    the same archive.

    Wrong argument types raise TypeError: a non-:class:`HPBArchive`
    archive, a non-tuple ``archive.items`` field, an item that is not an
    :class:`HPB`, a non-tuple index sequence or a non-integer
    (including boolean) index. An empty archive or index tuple, a
    structurally illegal nested bundle, a count at or above ``2**64``,
    indices that are not strictly increasing and unique, or an index
    outside ``0 <= i < total`` raises ValueError.
    """
    if not isinstance(archive, HPBArchive):
        raise TypeError(
            "archive must be an HPBArchive instance"
        )
    if not isinstance(indices, tuple):
        raise TypeError("indices must be a tuple")
    items = _check_hpap_archive_items(archive.items)
    try:
        total = len(items)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
    if total > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
    try:
        index_count = len(indices)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many indices") from None
    if index_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("indices must be non-empty")
    previous = -1
    for index in indices:
        if not isinstance(index, int) or isinstance(index, bool):
            raise TypeError("each index must be an integer")
        if index <= previous:
            raise ValueError("indices must be strictly increasing and unique")
        if index < 0 or index >= total:
            raise ValueError("index out of range")
        previous = index

    levels = _hpap_levels(items)

    siblings: list[bytes] = []
    positions = set(indices)
    for level in levels[:-1]:
        width = len(level)
        padded = level if width % 2 == 0 else level + level[-1:]
        next_positions = set()
        for position in sorted(positions):
            if width % 2 == 1 and position == width - 1:
                # Odd tail with no companion: the tree pairs it with itself.
                pass
            elif (position ^ 1) in positions:
                # The companion is itself a disclosed node; nothing to send.
                pass
            else:
                siblings.append(padded[position ^ 1])
            next_positions.add(position // 2)
        positions = next_positions

    root = levels[-1][0]
    proof_bundles = tuple(items[index] for index in indices)
    proof = HPAP(
        indices=tuple(indices),
        total=total,
        bundles=proof_bundles,
        siblings=tuple(siblings),
    )
    return HPAP_ROOT_TAG + _hp_u64(total) + root, proof


def _validate_hpap_structure(
    proof: object,
) -> tuple[
    tuple[int, ...],
    int,
    tuple[HPB, ...],
    tuple[bytes, ...],
]:
    """Type- and structure-check an HPAP, returning its fields.

    Only the container structure is checked: the bundles themselves are
    neither encoded nor verified here (encoding happens in the leaf
    recomputation and verification is :func:`verify_hpb`'s job). The
    bounds are ``0 < total < 2**64``, a non-empty ``indices`` tuple of
    strictly increasing indices in ``0 <= i < total`` and a siblings
    tuple whose entries are exactly 32 bytes. Wrong field types raise
    TypeError; illegal bounds or shapes raise ValueError. The two count
    couplings — bundles pairing one-to-one with indices and the sibling
    count the compact walk derives from ``total`` and ``indices`` — are
    not judged here: :func:`check_hpap` reports either mismatch as
    ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(proof, HPAP):
        raise TypeError("proof must be an HPAP instance")
    indices = proof.indices
    total = proof.total
    bundles = proof.bundles
    siblings = proof.siblings
    if not isinstance(indices, tuple):
        raise TypeError("proof.indices must be a tuple")
    if not isinstance(total, int) or isinstance(total, bool):
        raise TypeError("proof.total must be an integer")
    if not isinstance(bundles, tuple):
        raise TypeError("proof.bundles must be a tuple")
    if not isinstance(siblings, tuple):
        raise TypeError("proof.siblings must be a tuple")

    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("proof.total must be positive")
    if total > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
    try:
        index_count = len(indices)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many indices") from None
    if index_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("proof.indices must be non-empty")

    previous = -1
    for index in indices:
        if not isinstance(index, int) or isinstance(index, bool):
            raise TypeError("proof.indices entries must be integers")
        if index <= previous:
            raise ValueError(
                "proof.indices must be strictly increasing and unique"
            )
        if index < 0 or index >= total:
            raise ValueError("proof.indices entry out of range")
        previous = index

    for bundle in bundles:
        if not isinstance(bundle, HPB):
            raise TypeError(
                "proof.bundles entries must be HPB instances"
            )

    for sibling in siblings:
        if not isinstance(sibling, bytes):
            raise TypeError("proof.siblings entries must be bytes")
    try:
        len(siblings)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many siblings") from None
    for sibling in siblings:
        if len(sibling) != HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE:
            raise ValueError(
                "proof.siblings entries must be exactly 32 bytes"
            )
    return indices, total, bundles, siblings


def check_hpap(
    proof: HPAP,
    signature: AggregateSignature,
    key: SigningDKGResult,
) -> bool:
    """Rebuild a proof's Merkle root and verify its bundles and root signature.

    The root ``signature`` and ``key`` structures are checked first.
    Each disclosed bundle's leaf digest is then recomputed from its
    position and the bundle exactly as in :func:`make_hpap`, and the
    root is rebuilt level by level while consuming ``proof.siblings`` in
    ascending level order and left to right within a level: the current
    level holds the digests of the proven nodes at their current
    positions, paired left to right; when a companion is itself a
    current-level node its digest is used directly, when the node is the
    last member of an odd-width level it is paired with itself, and
    otherwise the next 32-byte entry of ``siblings`` is consumed. The
    current width contracts as ``(width + 1) // 2`` and the rebuild must
    consume every sibling exactly. Every disclosed bundle is then
    re-checked with :func:`verify_hpb` against ``key`` in index order,
    so each bundle's nested HP proof and every archive proof bundle it
    in turn discloses must verify, and the statement
    ``b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root`` is finally checked as
    ``signature``'s threshold Schnorr message via
    :func:`verify_signature` with the key's group parameters. Returns
    ``True`` only when the rebuild consumes every sibling exactly and
    reaches the single signed root, every bundle verifies against the
    key and the signature verifies; a well-formed proof whose bundles,
    indices, siblings, root or signature was tampered with — bundles
    swapped or altered, a bundle, index or sibling missing or extra, a
    misplaced sibling — or which is presented under another key, returns
    ``False`` rather than raising.

    A non-:class:`HPAP` or non-:class:`AggregateSignature` argument or
    any wrong field type (non-tuple indices/bundles/siblings, a
    non-integer ``total`` or index including booleans, a non-:class:`HPB`
    bundle or non-bytes sibling) raises TypeError; a non-positive or
    over-64-bit ``total``, empty indices, an index out of range or not
    strictly increasing, a sibling entry that is not exactly 32 bytes, or
    a structurally illegal bundle, signature or ``key`` raises ValueError,
    exactly as :func:`verify_hpb` and :func:`verify_signature` would.
    """
    indices, total, bundles, siblings = _validate_hpap_structure(proof)
    if not isinstance(signature, AggregateSignature):
        raise TypeError("signature must be an AggregateSignature instance")
    _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(signature)

    _result, public_key, field_prime, group_prime, generator = _check_signing_setup(key)
    _check_signing_dkg_structure(key)

    try:
        if len(bundles) != len(indices):
            return False
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive proof bundles") from None

    nodes = {
        index: _hpap_leaf(index, bundle)
        for index, bundle in zip(indices, bundles)
    }
    pending = iter(siblings)
    width = total
    while width > 1:
        next_nodes = {}
        for position in sorted(nodes):
            parent = position // 2
            if parent in next_nodes:
                continue
            if width % 2 == 1 and position == width - 1:
                # Odd tail with no companion: pair the node with itself.
                next_nodes[parent] = _hpap_node(
                    nodes[position], nodes[position]
                )
            elif (position ^ 1) in nodes:
                left = position if position % 2 == 0 else position ^ 1
                next_nodes[parent] = _hpap_node(
                    nodes[left], nodes[left ^ 1]
                )
            else:
                sibling = next(pending, None)
                if sibling is None:
                    # A sibling the walk needs is missing.
                    return False
                if position % 2 == 0:
                    next_nodes[parent] = _hpap_node(
                        nodes[position], sibling
                    )
                else:
                    next_nodes[parent] = _hpap_node(
                        sibling, nodes[position]
                    )
        nodes = next_nodes
        width = (width + 1) // 2

    if next(pending, None) is not None:
        # The rebuild must consume every sibling exactly.
        return False

    for bundle in bundles:
        if not verify_hpb(bundle, key):
            return False

    signed_message = (
        HPAP_ROOT_TAG
        + _hp_u64(total)
        + nodes[0]
    )
    return verify_signature(
        signed_message,
        signature,
        public_key,
        group_prime=group_prime,
        generator=generator,
        prime=field_prime,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical HPAP transport encoding and the proof-plus-root-signature
# bundle: the proof alone serializes as one self-delimiting,
# byte-for-byte reproducible byte string, and HPAPB carries it together
# with the aggregate threshold-Schnorr signature over its root statement
# — the same b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root message make_hpap returns —
# mirroring encode_hp and the HPB transport bundle one level down. Decoding
# restores structure only — the nested bundles go through decode_hpb, no
# bundle or signature is checked and no state is kept, so check_hpap
# through verify_hpapb remains the sole verifier afterwards.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

HPAP_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpap/v1"
HPAPB_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpapb/v1"


def encode_hpap(proof: HPAP) -> bytes:
    """Canonically encode an HPAP membership proof for transport or persistence.

    The encoding is the direct concatenation, in order, of the tag
    ``b"ts/hpap/v1"``, ``VARINT(total)``, the index count as a 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian integer, one ``VARINT(index)`` per proven leaf in
    the proof's strictly increasing order, the bundle count as a 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian integer, one frame per bundle — the 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian length ``len(E)`` followed by the raw bytes
    ``E = encode_hpb(bundle_value)`` (never empty) — and a 4-byte unsigned
    big-endian sibling item count followed by the raw 32-byte sibling
    digests concatenated directly in their original leaf-to-root,
    left-to-right order. A ``VARINT`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian body
    length followed by the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the
    single byte ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero). The
    integer and frame conventions are exactly those of :func:`encode_hp`.
    The indices must be non-empty, strictly increasing, unique and within
    ``0 <= i < total``, the bundle count must equal the index count, and
    the sibling count must be the unique one derived from ``total`` and
    the indices by the compact multi-proof walk.

    Only a structurally legal :class:`HPAP` is accepted — a non-:class:`HPAP`
    argument or wrong field types raise TypeError and illegal bounds, an
    empty index tuple, a bundle tuple that does not pair one-to-one with
    the indices, a sibling that is not exactly 32 bytes, a sibling count
    other than the one ``total`` and the indices determine, a
    structurally illegal nested bundle or an over-long frame raises
    ValueError — but the bundles are not verified and no signature is
    involved: :func:`check_hpap` stays the way to verify a proof
    afterwards. The output for a given proof is unique and the encoding
    carries no network, storage or hidden state.
    """
    indices, total, bundles, siblings = _validate_hpap_structure(proof)
    try:
        if len(bundles) != len(indices):
            raise ValueError(
                "proof.bundles must pair one-to-one with proof.indices"
            )
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive proof bundles") from None
    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
        total, indices
    )
    if len(siblings) != required_siblings:
        raise ValueError(
            "proof.siblings count is not the one determined by total "
            "and indices"
        )
    if len(indices) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many indices")
    if len(siblings) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many siblings")

    encoded_bundles = []
    for position, bundle_value in enumerate(bundles):
        encoded_bundle = encode_hpb(bundle_value)
        if len(encoded_bundle) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise ValueError(
                f"hpap bundle {position + 1} encoding too long"
            )
        encoded_bundles.append(encoded_bundle)

    buffer = bytearray(HPAP_WIRE_TAG)
    buffer += _encode_varint(total)
    buffer += len(indices).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for index in indices:
        buffer += _encode_varint(index)
    buffer += len(encoded_bundles).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for encoded_bundle in encoded_bundles:
        buffer += len(encoded_bundle).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
        buffer += encoded_bundle
    buffer += len(siblings).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for sibling in siblings:
        buffer += sibling
    return bytes(buffer)


def decode_hpap(blob: bytes) -> HPAP:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpap`.

    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag ``b"ts/hpap/v1"``, the
    length-prefixed integer ``total`` (a 4-byte unsigned big-endian
    length followed by its shortest unsigned big-endian value, zero
    encoded as the single byte ``00``), the 4-byte non-zero index count
    followed by one canonical ``VARINT`` per strictly increasing index,
    the 4-byte bundle count (which must equal the index count) followed
    by that many non-empty bundle frames (a 4-byte non-zero length
    followed by bytes that :func:`decode_hpb` accepts), and the 4-byte
    sibling item count followed by exactly that many raw 32-byte sibling
    digests concatenated with no further framing, where the count must be
    the unique one derived from ``total`` and the disclosed indices. A
    non-bytes argument raises TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, an empty
    index list, a non-positive or over-64-bit ``total``, an index outside
    ``0 <= i < total``, indices that are not strictly increasing and
    unique, a bundle count that does not match the index count, an empty,
    truncated or non-canonical bundle frame, a missing or extra sibling
    relative to the count ``total`` and the indices require, a sibling
    section whose width is not exactly 32 bytes per item, a non-canonical
    integer (leading zero or over-long length), truncation, or trailing
    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded proof re-encodes to
    exactly the input bytes.

    Decoding only restores the structure: each nested bundle is decoded
    with :func:`decode_hpb` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
    signature). A structurally legal proof whose nested bundles do not
    verify is returned normally, and :func:`check_hpap` reports it as
    ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
    if not blob.startswith(HPAP_WIRE_TAG):
        raise ValueError("bad HPAP proof tag")
    offset = len(HPAP_WIRE_TAG)

    total, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="hpap proof total")
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("hpap proof total must be positive")
    if total > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("hpap proof total too large")

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof index count")
    index_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if index_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("hpap proof indices must be non-empty")
    indices = []
    for _ in range(index_count):
        index, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="hpap proof index")
        indices.append(index)

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof bundle count")
    bundle_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if bundle_count != index_count:
        raise ValueError(
            "hpap proof bundle count must match the index count"
        )
    bundles = []
    for position in range(bundle_count):
        encoded_bundle, offset = _read_archive_block(
            blob,
            offset,
            what=f"hpap proof bundle {position + 1}",
        )
        bundles.append(decode_hpb(encoded_bundle))

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof sibling count")
    sibling_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
        total, tuple(indices)
    )
    if sibling_count != required_siblings:
        raise ValueError(
            "hpap proof sibling count is not the one determined by total "
            "and indices"
        )
    siblings = []
    for _ in range(sibling_count):
        if offset + HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE > len(blob):
            raise ValueError("truncated hpap proof sibling")
        siblings.append(
            bytes(blob[offset:offset + HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE])
        )
        offset += HPAP_DIGEST_SIZE

    if offset != len(blob):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPAP proof")

    proof = HPAP(
        indices=tuple(indices),
        total=total,
        bundles=tuple(bundles),
        siblings=tuple(siblings),
    )
    _validate_hpap_structure(proof)
    if encode_hpap(proof) != blob:
        raise ValueError("non-canonical hpap proof encoding")
    return proof


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HPAPB:
    """A compact multi-bundle archive membership proof with its root signature.

    The fields, in order, are ``proof`` (an :class:`HPAP`) and
    ``signature`` (the :class:`AggregateSignature` on the proof's
    ``b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root`` statement, the exact message
    :func:`make_hpap` returns). The dataclass is frozen, positionally
    constructible and compared by value, and carries no network, storage
    or hidden state. Field types and bounds are not checked at
    construction time — :func:`encode_hpapb` checks the structure and
    :func:`verify_hpapb` is the way to test a bundle afterwards.
    """

    proof: HPAP
    signature: AggregateSignature


def encode_hpapb(bundle: HPAPB) -> bytes:
    """Canonically encode an hpap bundle for transport or persistence.

    The encoding is the direct concatenation, in order, of the tag
    ``b"ts/hpapb/v1"``, one 4-byte unsigned big-endian length frame whose
    body is exactly ``encode_hpap(bundle.proof)`` (never empty), and then
    the existing signature frame: ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the
    4-byte unsigned big-endian signer count and one ``VARINT(id)`` per
    ascending signer id — the same frame :func:`encode_hpb` appends.
    A ``VARINT`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian body length followed by
    the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the single byte
    ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero); ``R`` must be
    positive and ``z`` may be zero.

    Only a structurally legal :class:`HPAPB` is accepted — a non-bundle
    or non-:class:`HPAP` proof argument, or wrong proof/signature field
    types, raise TypeError and illegal proof structure (the exact bounds
    of :func:`encode_hpap`), a structurally illegal signature (a
    non-positive ``R``, a negative ``z``, an empty or
    non-strictly-increasing signer id tuple) or an over-long frame
    raises ValueError — but the proof is not verified and the signature
    is not checked against the root: :func:`verify_hpapb` stays the way
    to verify a bundle afterwards. The output for a given bundle is
    unique, stateless and does not parse the nested bundle frames.
    """
    if not isinstance(bundle, HPAPB):
        raise TypeError("bundle must be an HPAPB instance")
    if not isinstance(bundle.proof, HPAP):
        raise TypeError("bundle.proof must be an HPAP instance")
    encoded_proof = encode_hpap(bundle.proof)
    signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(bundle.signature)
    if len(encoded_proof) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("hpap proof encoding too long")
    if signer_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many signer ids")

    buffer = bytearray(HPAPB_WIRE_TAG)
    buffer += len(encoded_proof).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    buffer += encoded_proof
    buffer += _encode_varint(bundle.signature.R)
    buffer += _encode_varint(bundle.signature.z)
    buffer += signer_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for signer_id in bundle.signature.signer_ids:
        buffer += _encode_varint(signer_id)
    return bytes(buffer)


def decode_hpapb(blob: bytes) -> HPAPB:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpapb`.

    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag ``b"ts/hpapb/v1"``, a
    4-byte non-zero frame length followed by bytes that
    :func:`decode_hpap` accepts, and then the signature frame: the
    length-prefixed integers ``R`` and ``z`` with ``R`` positive, the
    4-byte non-zero signer count and exactly that many strictly
    increasing positive signer ids. A non-bytes argument raises
    TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, a zero or over-long proof frame
    length, a non-canonical nested proof, a zero ``R``, a non-canonical
    integer (leading zero or over-long length), a zero signer count, a
    non-positive or non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing
    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded bundle re-encodes to
    exactly the input bytes.

    Decoding only restores the structure: the nested proof is decoded
    with :func:`decode_hpap` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
    signature) and the root signature is not checked. A structurally
    legal bundle whose nested bundles do not verify or whose signature
    does not sign the root is returned normally, and
    :func:`verify_hpapb` reports it as ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
    if not blob.startswith(HPAPB_WIRE_TAG):
        raise ValueError("bad hpap bundle tag")
    offset = len(HPAPB_WIRE_TAG)

    encoded_proof, offset = _read_archive_block(
        blob, offset, what="HPAPB proof"
    )
    proof = decode_hpap(encoded_proof)

    signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
        blob, offset, what="HPAPB"
    )
    if offset != len(blob):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPAPB")

    bundle = HPAPB(proof=proof, signature=signature)
    if encode_hpapb(bundle) != blob:
        raise ValueError("non-canonical hpap bundle encoding")
    return bundle


def verify_hpapb(bundle: HPAPB, key: SigningDKGResult) -> bool:
    """Verify a bundle exactly as :func:`check_hpap` would.

    This is a convenience wrapper over
    ``check_hpap(bundle.proof, bundle.signature, key)``: the Merkle root
    is rebuilt from the proof, every disclosed bundle is re-checked with
    :func:`verify_hpb` against ``key`` and the signature verified on the
    exact statement :func:`make_hpap` returns,
    ``b"hpap/r" || U64(total) || root``. Returns ``True`` only when all
    of them hold; a well-formed bundle with a tampered bundle, index,
    sibling or signature, a bundle swapped or altered, a missing or extra
    sibling, or one presented under another key, returns ``False``.

    A non-:class:`HPAPB` argument raises TypeError; illegal nested proof,
    bundle, signature or key structure raises TypeError/ValueError,
    exactly as :func:`check_hpap` does.
    """
    if not isinstance(bundle, HPAPB):
        raise TypeError("bundle must be an HPAPB instance")
    return check_hpap(bundle.proof, bundle.signature, key)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical HPB archive: several whole HPB membership-proof transport
# bundles kept in their original order as one non-empty tuple, with one
# aggregate threshold-Schnorr signature authenticating both the bytes and
# their order over the archive's canonical framing. Mirrors the existing
# HBPB archive layer one level down: the value is frozen and stateless, the
# message can be taken through the two-round threshold signing flow as is,
# and decoding restores structure only — every nested bundle goes through
# decode_hpb, no bundle or signature is checked and no state is kept, so
# verify_hpba remains the sole verifier afterwards.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

HPBA_MESSAGE_TAG = b"ts/hpba/m1"
HPBA_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpba/w1"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HPBArchive:
    """A non-empty ordered archive of HPB bundles with one outer signature.

    The fields, in order, are ``items`` — a non-empty tuple of
    :class:`HPB` values in archive order — and ``signature`` — the
    threshold Schnorr :class:`AggregateSignature` on
    :func:`hpba_message` of the items and the verifying public key.
    The dataclass is frozen, positionally constructible and compared by
    value; neither field has a default, the items keep their order and
    the archive carries no network, storage or hidden state. Neither
    field is checked at construction time — :func:`hpba_message`
    requires structurally legal items and :func:`verify_hpba` is the
    way to test an archive against a key afterwards.
    """

    items: tuple[HPB, ...]
    signature: AggregateSignature


def hpba_message(
    items: tuple[HPB, ...], public_key: int
) -> bytes:
    """Encode the canonical message the threshold key signs for an archive.

    The message is, in order, the tag ``b"ts/hpba/m1"``, the 32-byte
    ``SHA256`` digest of the canonical framing ``C`` and
    ``V(public_key)`` — a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by
    the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the single byte
    ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero). With
    ``E_i = encode_hpb(items[i])`` and ``n`` the item count, ``C`` is
    built in tuple order as ``U32(n) || Σ(U32(len(E_i)) || E_i)``;
    every ``U32`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian integer, the frames
    carry no separators and ``E_i`` is the existing canonical transport
    encoding of the bundle. The message carries no signature and keeps
    no state, and can be taken through the two-round threshold signing
    flow as is.

    ``items`` must be a non-empty tuple of structurally legal
    :class:`HPB` values exactly as :func:`encode_hpb` requires and
    ``public_key`` a non-boolean non-negative integer. Wrong field or
    nested field types raise TypeError — a non-tuple items sequence, an
    item that is not an :class:`HPB`, or a non-integer (including
    boolean) public key; an empty items tuple, an illegal nested
    bundle, a negative public key or an over-long encoding raises
    ValueError.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
    if not isinstance(public_key, int) or isinstance(public_key, bool):
        raise TypeError("public_key must be an integer")

    try:
        item_count = len(items)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
    if item_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
    if item_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
    if public_key < 0:
        raise ValueError("public_key must be non-negative")

    # Encode every bundle first — each call raises TypeError/ValueError
    # for an illegal bundle exactly as the bundle codec does — and only
    # then frame the results, so a single illegal item aborts the whole
    # message.
    frames = []
    for index, item in enumerate(items):
        encoded = encode_hpb(item)
        if len(encoded) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise ValueError(
                f"HPB archive item {index + 1} encoding too long"
            )
        frames.append(encoded)

    framing = bytearray(item_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False))
    for encoded in frames:
        framing += len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
        framing += encoded
    return (
        HPBA_MESSAGE_TAG
        + hashlib.sha256(bytes(framing)).digest()
        + _encode_varint(public_key)
    )


def verify_hpba(
    archive: HPBArchive, key: SigningDKGResult
) -> bool:
    """Verify an archive of HPB bundles against the threshold key.

    ``archive`` must be a structurally legal :class:`HPBArchive` and
    ``key`` a legal :class:`SigningDKGResult`. The outer signature and
    the key structure are checked first, as is the structure of every
    item, so an illegal outer signature or key is never masked by a bad
    nested bundle: a non-:class:`HPBArchive` argument, a non-tuple
    ``items`` field, a non-:class:`HPB` element or a
    non-:class:`SigningDKGResult` ``key`` raises TypeError, and an
    empty items tuple, an illegal outer signature structure, an illegal
    key structure or any structurally illegal nested bundle raises
    ValueError.

    Every bundle is then passed to :func:`verify_hpb` in archive
    order, so each disclosed HP membership proof, the HBPB bundles it
    carries and its root signature must verify under ``key``; the
    canonical :func:`hpba_message` of the items and
    ``key.public_key`` is finally checked as the outer signature's
    threshold Schnorr message via :func:`verify_signature` with the
    key's group parameters. Returns ``True`` only when every
    per-bundle check and the outer signature check pass; a structurally
    legal archive whose nested bundle or outer signature does not match
    — including deleting, inserting, reordering or substituting a
    bundle, tampering with the outer signature, or presenting the
    archive under another key — returns ``False`` rather than raising.
    The function is stateless.
    """
    if not isinstance(archive, HPBArchive):
        raise TypeError(
            "archive must be an HPBArchive instance"
        )
    items = archive.items
    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
    # Check the outer signature and the key before any nested bundle is
    # examined, so a bad bundle can never mask an illegal outer
    # signature or key; structurally validate every nested bundle too,
    # exactly as the single-bundle verifier validates its proof.
    _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(archive.signature)
    _result, public_key, field_prime, group_prime, generator = _check_signing_setup(key)
    _check_signing_dkg_structure(key)
    try:
        item_count = len(items)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
    if item_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
    for item in items:
        encode_hpb(item)

    if not all(verify_hpb(item, key) for item in items):
        return False
    message = hpba_message(items, public_key)
    return verify_signature(
        message,
        archive.signature,
        public_key,
        group_prime=group_prime,
        generator=generator,
        prime=field_prime,
    )

    field types. An empty items tuple, an over-long count or frame,
    any structural error a bundle would raise on its own, or an
    illegal outer signature structure raises ValueError. The output
    for a given archive is unique and the encoding carries no
    network, storage or hidden state.
    """
    if not isinstance(archive, HPBArchive):
        raise TypeError(
            "archive must be an HPBArchive instance"
        )
    items = archive.items
    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
    try:
        item_count = len(items)
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
    if item_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
    if item_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
    signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(archive.signature)
    if signer_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many signer ids")

    # Encode every item first — each call raises TypeError/ValueError
    # for an illegal bundle exactly as the single-bundle codec does —
    # and only then frame the results, so a single illegal item aborts
    # the whole archive.
    frames = []
    for index, item in enumerate(items):
        encoded = encode_hpb(item)
        if len(encoded) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise ValueError(
                f"HPB archive item {index + 1} encoding too long"
            )
        frames.append(encoded)

    buffer = bytearray(HPBA_WIRE_TAG)
    buffer += item_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for encoded in frames:
        buffer += len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
        buffer += encoded
    buffer += _encode_varint(archive.signature.R)
    buffer += _encode_varint(archive.signature.z)
    buffer += signer_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for signer_id in archive.signature.signer_ids:
        buffer += _encode_varint(signer_id)
    return bytes(buffer)


def decode_hpba(blob: bytes) -> HPBArchive:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpba`.

    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag
    ``b"ts/hpba/w1"``, a 4-byte unsigned big-endian non-zero item
    count ``n``, then exactly ``n`` frames, each a 4-byte unsigned
    big-endian non-zero byte length followed by the exact canonical
    encoding of one :class:`HPB` that :func:`decode_hpb` accepts,
    and finally the outer signature frame: the length-prefixed integers
    ``R`` and ``z`` with ``R`` positive, the 4-byte non-zero signer
    count ``k`` and then exactly ``k`` strictly increasing positive
    signer ids. The bundles are restored in their original order as a
    tuple; they are neither sorted nor matched against one another or
    against the outer signature, and no signature is verified —
    :func:`verify_hpba` judges the archive afterwards. A non-bytes
    argument raises TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, a zero item
    count, a zero or over-long frame length, a declared count that does
    not match the number of frames, a nested bundle encoding that is
    illegal or non-canonical (including a frame that would not
    re-encode byte for byte), a zero ``R``, a non-canonical integer
    (leading zero or over-long length), a zero signer count, a
    non-positive or non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing
    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded archive re-encodes
    to exactly the input bytes.

    Decoding only restores structure: every nested bundle is decoded
    with :func:`decode_hpb` (which verifies no proof and checks no
    signature) and the outer signature is not checked. A structurally
    legal archive whose bundles do not verify or whose outer signature
    does not sign the bundles is returned normally, and
    :func:`verify_hpba` reports it as ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
    if not blob.startswith(HPBA_WIRE_TAG):
        raise ValueError("bad HPB archive tag")
    offset = len(HPBA_WIRE_TAG)

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated HPB archive item count")
    item_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if item_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("HPB archive items must be non-empty")

    items = []
    for index in range(item_count):
        frame, offset = _read_archive_block(
            blob,
            offset,
            what=f"HPB archive item {index + 1}",
        )
        items.append(decode_hpb(frame))

    signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
        blob, offset, what="HPB archive"
    )
    if offset != len(blob):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPB archive")

    archive = HPBArchive(items=tuple(items), signature=signature)
    if encode_hpba(archive) != blob:
        raise ValueError("non-canonical HPB archive encoding")
    return archive

def _read_archive_block(
    stream: bytes, offset: int, *, what: str
) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
    """Read one 4-byte-length-prefixed frame body at ``offset``.

    The same wire rules as :func:`_read_audit_proof_block` with a
    non-empty body, but the error messages are phrased purely in the
    caller's ``what`` terms.
    """
    if offset + 4 > len(stream):
        raise ValueError(f"truncated {what} length")
    length = int.from_bytes(stream[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if length == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} must be non-empty")
    if offset + length > len(stream):
        raise ValueError(f"truncated {what}")
    return bytes(stream[offset:offset + length]), offset + length


def decode_audit_proof(payload: bytes) -> AuditProof:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_audit_proof`.

    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag
    ``b"thresholdsign/audit-proof/v1"``, the length-prefixed integers ``i``
    and ``n`` (each a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by its
    shortest unsigned big-endian value, zero encoded as the single byte
    ``00``), the message frame (a 4-byte length, possibly zero, followed by
    the raw message), the receipt frame (a 4-byte non-zero length followed by
    the raw receipt bytes), the 4-byte path count and then exactly that many
    raw 32-byte path entries. A non-bytes argument raises TypeError; a wrong
    or missing tag, an empty receipt, an out-of-range ``i``, an over-64-bit
    ``n``, a non-canonical integer (leading zero or over-long length),
    truncation, trailing bytes, or a path count that does not equal
    ``(n - 1).bit_length()`` (including entries that are not exactly 32
    bytes) raises ValueError. A successfully decoded proof re-encodes to
    exactly the input bytes.

    Decoding only restores the structure: the receipt is stored opaque and
    is neither parsed nor verified, no signature is checked and no state is
    kept. A structurally legal proof whose receipt does not match its
    message or whose sealing signature is invalid is returned normally, and
    :func:`check_proof` reports it as ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(payload, bytes):
        raise TypeError("payload must be bytes")
    if not payload.startswith(AUDIT_PROOF_WIRE_TAG):
        raise ValueError("bad audit proof tag")
    offset = len(AUDIT_PROOF_WIRE_TAG)

    index, offset = _read_varint(payload, offset, what="audit proof i")
    count, offset = _read_varint(payload, offset, what="audit proof n")
    message, offset = _read_audit_proof_block(
        payload, offset, what="message", allow_empty=True
    )
    receipt, offset = _read_audit_proof_block(payload, offset, what="receipt")

    if offset + 4 > len(payload):
        raise ValueError("truncated audit proof path count")
    path_count = int.from_bytes(payload[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    path = []
    for _ in range(path_count):
        if offset + AUDIT_PROOF_DIGEST_SIZE > len(payload):
            raise ValueError("truncated audit proof path")
        path.append(bytes(payload[offset:offset + AUDIT_PROOF_DIGEST_SIZE]))
        offset += AUDIT_PROOF_DIGEST_SIZE
    if offset != len(payload):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after audit proof")

    proof = AuditProof(
        i=index,
        n=count,
        m=message,
        a=SigningAudit(payload=receipt),
        p=tuple(path),
    )
    _validate_audit_proof_structure(proof)
    if encode_audit_proof(proof) != payload:
        raise ValueError("non-canonical audit proof")

def _read_bundle_signature_frame(
    stream: bytes, offset: int, *, what: str
) -> tuple[AggregateSignature, int]:
    """Read one canonical bundle signature frame at ``offset``.

    The frame is ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the 4-byte non-zero signer
    count and then exactly that many strictly increasing positive
    ``VARINT(id)`` entries — the same rules
    :func:`decode_audit_proof_bundle` applies to its single signature.
    """
    R, offset = _read_varint(stream, offset, what=f"{what} signature R")
    z, offset = _read_varint(stream, offset, what=f"{what} signature z")
    if R == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} signature R must be positive")

    if offset + 4 > len(stream):
        raise ValueError(f"truncated {what} signer count")
    signer_count = int.from_bytes(stream[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if signer_count == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} must name at least one signer")

    signer_ids = []
    for _ in range(signer_count):
        signer_id, offset = _read_varint(
            stream, offset, what=f"{what} signer id"
        )
        if signer_id == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{what} signer ids must be positive")
        if signer_ids and signer_id <= signer_ids[-1]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what} signer ids must be strictly increasing and unique"
            )
        signer_ids.append(signer_id)
    return (
        AggregateSignature(R=R, z=z, signer_ids=tuple(signer_ids)),
        offset,
    )


def decode_audit_extension_proof_bundle(
    blob: bytes,
) -> AuditExtensionProofBundle:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_audit_extension_proof_bundle`.

    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag ``b"ts/aepb/v1"``, a
    4-byte non-zero frame length followed by bytes that
    :func:`decode_extension` accepts, and then the old and new signature
    frames, each the length-prefixed integers ``R`` and ``z``, the 4-byte
    non-zero signer count ``k`` and exactly ``k`` strictly increasing
    positive signer ids. A non-bytes argument raises TypeError; a wrong or
    missing tag, a zero or over-long proof frame length, a non-canonical
    nested proof, a zero ``R``, a non-canonical integer (leading zero or
    over-long length), a zero signer count, a non-positive or
    non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing bytes raises
    ValueError. A successfully decoded bundle re-encodes to exactly the
    input bytes.

    Decoding only restores the structure: the nested proof is decoded
    with :func:`decode_extension` (which keeps the leaf digests opaque
    and verifies nothing) and neither signature is checked. A
    structurally legal bundle whose signatures do not match its roots is
    returned normally, and
    :func:`verify_audit_extension_proof_bundle` reports it as ``False``.
    """
    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
    if not blob.startswith(AUDIT_EXTENSION_PROOF_BUNDLE_WIRE_TAG):
        raise ValueError("bad audit extension proof bundle tag")
    offset = len(AUDIT_EXTENSION_PROOF_BUNDLE_WIRE_TAG)

    encoded_proof, offset = _read_audit_proof_block(
        blob, offset, what="audit extension proof bundle proof"
    )
    proof = decode_extension(encoded_proof)

    old_signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
        blob, offset, what="audit extension proof bundle old"
    )
    new_signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
        blob, offset, what="audit extension proof bundle new"
    )
    if offset != len(blob):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after audit extension proof bundle")

    bundle = AuditExtensionProofBundle(
        proof=proof,
        old_signature=old_signature,

60	def build_framing(items) -> bytes:
61	    """Independently build C straight from the spec."""
62	    out = bytearray(u32(len(items)))
63	    for item in items:
64	        encoded = encode_hpb(item)
65	        out += u32(len(encoded))
66	        out += encoded

71	    """Independently build the archive message straight from the spec."""
72	    framing = build_framing(items)

"""Tests for the non-empty order-preserving archive of whole HPB
membership-proof bundles and its outer threshold-Schnorr signature:
HPBArchive / hpba_message / verify_hpba."""

import dataclasses
import hashlib
import unittest
from dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError

from thresholdsign import (
    AggregateSignature,
    HP,
    HPB,
    HPBArchive,
    encode_hpb,
    hpba_message,
    verify_hpb,
    verify_hpba,
